advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the footer lockstep comment to enumerate the backoff-skip no-op case and reflect the intended guard.
evidence: 856: # Keep the mcp component marker in lockstep with the global one on a COMPLETE deploy (the mcp
857: # block may have been a no-op this tick because nothing under $MCP_PATHS changed).
advisory.finding: The footer's lockstep comment ("the mcp block may have been a no-op this tick because nothing under $MCP_PATHS changed") does not account for the case where the mcp block was a no-op because its backoff window was open despite a real pending delta, so the stated invariant ("a later tick would diff from a stale mcp_deployed") is used to justify a write that is incorrect in the backoff case.
scenarios: Reviewer relies on the comment's enumeration of no-op causes, which omits backoff-skip.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not advance BOT_SHA_FILE at the footer when the bot was skipped by an active bot backoff window without deploying.
evidence: 682: if bot_backoff_active; then
683:   log "review-bot backoff active for $TARGET (fail #$bo_cnt); next bot attempt at $bo_next"
688: (no bot_deferred set on the backoff-skip branch, so it stays 0)
807: if [ "$bot_deferred" = 1 ]; then exit 0; fi
860: echo "$TARGET" > "$BOT_SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv "$BOT_SHA_FILE.tmp" "$BOT_SHA_FILE"
684: elif changed_range "$bot_deployed" "$TARGET" "$BOT_PATHS" — next tick sees bot_deployed==TARGET and never redeploys
698: if mcp_backoff_active && changed_range ... then log "mcp backoff active"
701: if ! mcp_backoff_active && changed_range ... (deploy body only runs when backoff NOT active)
859: echo "$TARGET" > "$MCP_SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv "$MCP_SHA_FILE.tmp" "$MCP_SHA_FILE" (footer, unconditional)
856-858: comment claims footer keeps mcp 'in lockstep ... because nothing under $MCP_PATHS changed' — but it also fires when mcp DID have a change and was skipped by backoff
blocking.finding: On a tick where the review-bot is skipped due to an active bot backoff window (bot_backoff_active true, not a deferral) but a bot change is pending, `bot_deferred` stays 0, so the tick reaches the success footer and writes `$TARGET` into `BOT_SHA_FILE`. This records the bot as deployed at a target it never deployed (it is in backoff), so the next tick computes `changed_range "$TARGET" "$TARGET"` = false and the failed target is silently never retried once the backoff window elapses.
merged_from: Symmetrically, on a tick where the mcp path is skipped because its backoff window is open (`mcp_backoff_active` true) but the bot deploys or is idle (no deferral), the tick reaches the footer and writes `$TARGET` into `MCP_SHA_FILE`, marking mcp as deployed at a target it was throttled from deploying. The next tick then computes `changed_range "$TARGET" "$TARGET"` = false for MCP_PATHS and never retries the failed mcp deploy after the backoff elapses.
scenarios: Bot deploy fails (records BACKOFF_FILE), backoff window still open on a later tick, a bot change is still pending, mcp has no pending change so no deferral occurs — footer marks bot as deployed at the un-deployed TARGET.
blocking.suggested_fix: Only write BOT_SHA_FILE at the footer when the bot actually deployed or was already at TARGET (e.g. gate the footer write on `bot_deployed = $TARGET`, which deploy_review_bot sets, rather than writing $TARGET unconditionally).

evidence: Tick 2 block: `second = _run(mcp_box)` then only `assert not any("compose-up-" in c or "compose-build-" in c for c in second_cmds)` with no positive liveness assertion for tick 2

Contrast: test_repeated_deferred_ticks_do_not_redeploy_mcp_every_time DOES anchor tick 2 with `assert "AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED" in second.stdout + second.stderr` before its absence checks, and test_mcp_backoff_window... anchors tick 2 with `assert "mcp backoff active" in second.stdout + second.stderr`
Tick 1 liveness anchors (compose-up-, mcp-unhealthy) do not establish that the SECOND _run reached the bot gate
blocking.finding: In test_a_failed_mcp_deploy_does_not_redeploy_the_bot_every_tick, the tick-2 absence assertion (bot not redeployed) has no liveness anchor proving tick 2 actually ran and reached the review-bot deploy gate. Unlike the sibling tests, tick 2 asserts only `not any("compose-up-" or "compose-build-")` with no positive check that the tick executed and evaluated the bot block. If tick 2 exited early for any unrelated reason (e.g. lock, an early guard), the absence assertion passes vacuously — the exact fail-open shape the other tests guard against on their second ticks.
scenarios: A regression that causes tick 2 to exit before the review-bot gate would leave this test green while the bot-deployed-sha protection is silently broken
blocking.suggested_fix: Before the tick-2 absence assertion, assert a positive signal that tick 2 ran and evaluated the bot gate — e.g. assert the bot-deployed-sha marker equals TARGET (so the gate saw the bot already deployed), or assert tick 2 emitted an expected log line proving it reached the component-delta stage.
